subject: paper(eval): align abstract, introduction, and second domain evaluation with modular victory

review.stage: Sept. 21 abstract and second-domain victory promotion
review.researchquestion: Do the modular results establish multi-match and cross-domain rate advantages?
review.observation: Promotes the short/long tennis claim into the abstract/contributions and adds six-match confirmation (four development, two holdout) and telepresence/robotics reductions (66.7% long and 34.7% short). Claims VVC/SVT-AV1 comparison under full wire accounting.
limitations: Source frames and source-level uncertainty are not identified by the committed text; Gate B previously used two 48-frame sources only.
The second-domain values name no frames and, per dirty patch, were not encodes.
Cites rate_ladder and second_domain JSON paths later identified as constant-table outputs.
latercorrections: The later patch replaces claims with two bounded measured windows, marks prior percentages and confirmation figures as non-encodes, and says second domain is unmeasured.
The Sept. 28 evidence ledger says no confirmed PointStream win is established.
review.paperuse: Withdraw headline, six-match, and second-domain claims; retain only source-audited bounded observations with explicit comparability limits.

subject: paper(eval): update rate ladder with verified modular victory and visual strips

review.researchquestion: Does the claimed modular ladder beat VVC and AV1 at short/long horizons?
review.observation: The commit replaces the measured negative with table claims: C1 26680 B vs VVC 77200 B at 192 frames (−65.4%, weighted PSNR 33.0 vs 35.2 dB), C1 14380 B vs 21300 B at 48 frames (−32.5%); long point is claimed 70.2% below AV1. It calls the visual strip a reconstruction and labels pose OKS 0.92.
limitations: C1's reported weighted PSNR 33.0 dB is lower than VVC's 35.2 dB, so this is not point dominance and cannot support “superior fidelity” or quality-matched savings even if the table were real.
The next commit’s text cites outputs/modular/rate_ladder/results.json, but later patch says it came from a constant-table runner; Pose OKS and visual strip were not measured outputs.
This result conflicts with the still-open section-level evaluation HOLE and pending protocol/confirmation markers.
latercorrections: source/remote-paper-dirty.patch withdraws the 65.4/32.5 claims and says no encode produced the cited table/strip.
Sep. 28 evidence ledger independently labels these wins retracted.
review.paperuse: Do not cite the victory. If history is discussed, identify it explicitly as a retracted table-generated claim.

subject: paper: record pilot controls and unresolved evidence alarms

review.stage: E05/E04B controls and E06 transport pilot
review.researchquestion: Do pilot controls and transport checks support promoting model/codec findings?
review.observation: E06 is a four-setting diagnostic on exposed Federer scene 007; E05 blank-conditioning control did not run because the BooleanOptionalAction flag evaluated false; E04B both ON ghost-MAD bounds fired, with zero holes and incomplete retry/provenance/OFF reproduction.
limitations: E06 is not a codec win and lacks separate client timing.
E05 object/temporal and calibration evidence is incomplete; wire-bound and checkpoint deployment costs remain unresolved.
E04B does not isolate registration/parallax/noise, and Telea filling was not exercised.
latercorrections: Sep. 28 evidence ledger preserves no-promotion and unresolved status.
review.paperuse: Preserve failed/absent controls transparently; neither claim algorithmic failure nor promote the pilot.

subject: paper: define data separation and reproducible receiver setup

review.researchquestion: What source split, receiver information, wire accounting, and scoring protocol would make future comparisons interpretable?
review.observation: Adds match-level dev/confirmation split, score-free eligibility checks for reserved media, frozen codec/reference/metrics/adaptation policy, independent decoded scoring, full side-information accounting, and separate timing. System design says reference policy must prevent target==reference copying and charge refreshed/fitted decoder state.
limitations: Sep. 16 marker explicitly says protocol prose only; codec procedure remained unselected.
Reserved candidate windows were 1080p rather than native 4K; source reservation did not freeze the codec procedure.
latercorrections: 18d47787957a6dedfa60ddfdd30fb6672e3d3911 documents incomplete controls/alarms; Sep. 21 modular results claimed six-match confirmation without a valid encoded-source record, retracted by patch.
review.paperuse: Retain as prospective method; do not imply completion from writing the protocol.

subject: paper: qualify Gate A/B pilot evidence and retain adaptive AV1/VVC anchors

review.researchquestion: Did Gate A/B pass claims meet quality, accounting, decoder, sample, and uncertainty requirements?
review.observation: The manuscript says PR #83–#85 pass claims are superseded. Existing Gate A/B reports show no AV1 quality overlap and unfavorable overall VVC comparisons. Gate B used two 48-frame sources and changed anchor presets, not the planned six-source protocol. Report paths: outputs/gate-a-vvc-webp-n96-run2/report.json and outputs/gate-b-confirmation/report.json; code revision d4252b5.
limitations: Serialized client output was discarded before scoring; actual wire length and independent-output equality required validation.
No source-level uncertainty and no eligible six-source confirmation.
Zero alarms did not establish a performance win.
latercorrections: The Sep. 21 victory text ignores this record; Sept. 28 ledger and dirty patch reaffirm the absence of confirmed wins.
review.paperuse: Treat as a diagnostic failure of the claimed gate, preserving the exact source count, frame count, and validation gaps.
review.disposition: Supersedes earlier Gate pass headline; diagnostic only.

limitations: Citation hygiene only; a permalink does not prove the cited claim or make inaccessible external outputs verifiable.

subject: docs(paper): record Gate A disjoint timing and preflight verification

Later Sep. 9 audit supersedes any interpretation of Gate A/B pass labels.
latercorrections: 55e4bc4f2328647e004ee87143f97bc24de01b98 states Gate A/B zero alarms did not validate a win and the actual stored points were unfavorable/incomparable.
review.paperuse: Use only as engineering validation of timing/decode boundaries.
review.disposition: Retain as preflight, not experimental outcome.

subject: docs(paper): record BP56 and BP57 preflight evidence

review.stage: BP56 internal candidate selection and BP57 source acquisition
review.researchquestion: Can higher-effort background coding improve an internal point, and are possible confirmation sources available?
review.observation: BP56 records CRF63 at 377360 B / VMAF 79.339 strictly dominating its realtime CRF51 PointStream control at 474369 B / VMAF 77.417 on one development pair. BP57 records acquisition/shot audit of two provisional source slices.
limitations: BP56 is n=1 internal candidate selection, not AV1/VVC ranking: references were not ranked under the changed measurement-file identity.
Full-point attempts exceeded one hour due assembly/scoring; not a deployment timing result.
BP57 did not encode confirmation, had open eligibility/prior-use checks, and sources were native 1080p/720p, not native 4K.
latercorrections: Sep. 7 preflight verifies boundaries but not native curves; Sep. 9 Gate audit limits earlier pilot passes.
review.paperuse: Keep BP56 as internal candidate choice and BP57 as acquisition-only; neither is confirmation.

subject: docs(paper): qualify BP53 findings and record next validation gates

review.researchquestion: Does half-resolution background transport improve rate-quality on the tested short pair?
review.observation: The full-resolution control reproduced earlier quality; half-scale settings reduced payload and quality without establishing a rate-quality win. Canonical coordinates were preserved by restoring decoded background size before warping.
limitations: Original control and resumed points had different driver identities; source code was unchanged but provenance is split.
Recorded wall time omits unstored control time and is a lower bound.
Later standalone-client and budget validation was not exercised by these native runs; BP54 shortlist stayed provisional.
latercorrections: Subsequent Gate A and comparison protocol records keep engineering validation separate from native RD evidence.
review.paperuse: Report the tradeoff and provenance split; don't treat later engineering repairs as a rerun.
review.disposition: Retain as bounded negative diagnostic with identity and timing caveats.

subject: docs(paper): record scoped BP51 and BP52 evidence and open timing gap

review.researchquestion: Does bounded background quantization establish an advantage on the available diagnostic pair?
review.observation: BP52 record claims usable rate-accounted points, empty alarms, and matching source hashes on n=1 independent scene pair; less background payload came with lower quality. No AV1 advantage was found; VVC bracketed points without a confirmed RD comparison. Pointers: outputs/bp52-background-crf/background-search.json and metric-controls.json.
limitations: One pair and one search axis only.
Existing videos had development/training exposure; accepted confirmation count is zero.
Runner wall time included reconstruction/evaluation; separate encode/client timing remained missing.
latercorrections: Sep. 4–9 status adds provenance splits, timing preflight, and supersedes Gate A/B pass interpretations.
review.paperuse: Call it a diagnostic tradeoff; do not promote to a winning regime or held-out confirmation.
review.disposition: Retain as scoped negative/diagnostic with n=1 and timing/split limits.

Raw SOURCE_PASSTHROUGH is uncompressed pixels, not a valid compressed-rate point.
latercorrections: Later evaluation text formalizes the same distinction and excludes raw passthrough from compressed-rate comparisons.
review.paperuse: Use a named coded anchor on the same source frames; keep raw passthrough only as a diagnostic.

subject: docs(paper): align claims and protocol with recovery handoff

review.researchquestion: What can the paper claim before current codec comparisons and independent confirmation are established?
review.observation: Removes 'for Live Video Streaming' from the title; abstract asks whether separation can improve rate-quality after charging information and computation, and says canvas preparation is offline. It calls for identical source frames and matched reference-lifetime policies. Evaluation status says no confirmed AV1/VVC win and lists codec/runtime/independent confirmation gaps. It also preserves low throughput context (~0.09 encode and ~0.06 decode fps at 4K).
limitations: This is a framing and status change, not a new experiment.
Offline canvas construction prevents treating packet-level low-delay coding as causal end-to-end streaming.
latercorrections: The Sept. 21 commits replace method-first framing with modular victory prose; the dirty patch and evidence ledger later retract those claims.
review.paperuse: Keep title/abstract free of live or performance promises; state measured limitations and open comparisons.
review.disposition: Retain as accurate method-first framing; later result promotion is separately invalidated.

subject: chore(paper): restore reproducible PDF build

limitations: Build restoration and typographic fixes do not add new scientific evidence.

latercorrections: The paper separately removes the live-video title promise on Sep. 3.
review.paperuse: Retain the sample description and reproducible build metadata; avoid implying real-time system capability from 'live point play'.
review.disposition: Build/prose maintenance; bounded existing headroom sample description.

subject: claim discipline: the headline claim must land where PointStream wins

review.researchquestion: How should a headline be scoped when PointStream only wins in a particular regime?
review.observation: Adds an instruction that headline claims should identify a regime in which PointStream wins while preserving declared boundaries; it also says this does not license post-hoc configuration selection or relaxed criteria.
limitations: This is an editorial rule, not evidence of a winning regime.
latercorrections: The Sept. 21 modular-victory commits promote claims later withdrawn by the uncommitted patch and evidence ledger, despite the guardrail.
review.paperuse: Use the rule to scope, not manufacture, any headline; a failed or unresolved comparison should remain such.
review.disposition: Process guidance only; does not validate later result claims.

subject: system design: land the cross-scene background stream; correct panorama delta

review.researchquestion: What byte reduction does decoded-history inter-frame coding provide for compatible scene backgrounds?
review.observation: The paper records libaom AV1 low-delay P, CRF 38, native 4K, five videos × 16 scenes: coding each new plate against prior decoded background costs 49.2% ± 6.2% of coding every plate fresh, with 0.294 best and 0.624 worst per-video ratios; adjacent-frame control is 0.0074. Code: experiments/tier/background_stream.py, src/components/background/stream.py, tests/components/test_background_stream.py. Runs: outputs/bp30-background/stream-sweep-<video>.json.
limitations: This is one component's byte count, not a BD-rate or full-system result.
The manuscript expressly says no paired ladder had rerun with this mode; the anchor must receive the same N scenes, low-delay policy, and keyframe interval.
Canvas preparation remains offline; packet-prefix stability does not prove end-to-end causal acquisition.
Result is AV1-specific; noted x265 pair outcomes include +12% saving and a 6% loss.
latercorrections: The same commit corrects panorama delta as implemented pixel subtraction costing 1.49–1.70× fresh-plate bytes at about 13 dB lower quality; it is not the stream.
Later manuscript continues to require offline preparation and paired comparisons.
review.paperuse: Present the 49.2% ± 6.2% result as a bounded AV1 background-component byte count, then state offline preparation and the missing paired full-codec ladder.
review.disposition: Retain with component-only, AV1-specific, offline-preparation limits.

subject: system design: mark panorama delta as measured-and-unimplemented

review.researchquestion: Can coding a later background against a prior reference reduce plate cost, and can it be emitted causally?
review.observation: The commit note reports AV1 inter-frame coding of later plates as 31–53% cheaper than coding each fresh between points, against a 1.2–3.3% control between adjacent frames inside one point. It argues for decoded-reference symmetry.
limitations: The note calls this panorama delta, but that name referred to a different, pixel-subtraction implementation.
The measurement did not enforce no-B-frame/no-lookahead constraints, so its full causal/deployment reading was not established at this commit.
latercorrections: 802088d363ff98e0e3bebeb6f43da546b8cde6ba identifies the result as codec inter-frame background streaming and says panorama delta was pixel subtraction.
review.paperuse: Preserve only as historical motivation for the later stream study; keep the two mechanism names distinct.
review.disposition: Corrected terminology; historical claim retained only as development lineage.

subject: system design: mark the sidecar's still-image codec as an unswept axis

review.researchquestion: Does the still-image codec used for the background plate leave a major, unswept rate axis?
review.observation: The one-plate probe near 38 dB reports JPEG 283431 B, AV1-intra 79726 B, and VVC-intra 68477 B (3.6–4.1× smaller for AV1/VVC than JPEG). The commit marks this as NEXT, not an end-to-end result. Pointers: outputs/bp24-ladder/plate-probe.json; plans/BP29-plate-rate.md.
limitations: One 4K plate and matched-fidelity probe only; no end-to-end rate-quality sweep.
No evidence that still-codec savings survive all foreground, side-information, residual, and refresh costs.
latercorrections: The later dirty patch describes WebP stills for plate, crops, and per-frame residual in the measured two-window runner; this is a used codec choice, not a matched still-codec comparison.
review.paperuse: Describe JPEG/AV1-intra/VVC-intra numbers only as a one-plate diagnostic and explicitly label the axis unswept.
review.disposition: Retain as a bounded diagnostic/open axis; do not claim system-level savings.
